Lilla is a very precious Aboriginal Outstation, the Community is about 15km from Wartarrka (Kings Canyon). 

This pilgrimage is an opportunity to drop into the simplicity of life and deep listening. Where we enter into a timeless space where we paint, make clap sticks, sing, have some body movement meditation practices and sit in circle with woman. Giving space for country to speak and be with the traditional owners. 

The places that you will visit in our time together will be Kings Canyon and Uluru.   

It’s a once in a life opportunity.

7 days and 6 nights

$3000 early bird till end of MARCH

From April $3300

# Sacred Returning Pilgrimage

  * Sat, 14 Oct 2023 9:30 am Sat, 21 Oct 2023 10:00 am
  * Google Calendar ICS

An invitation to connect with Country.

To the wide-open skies and desert fires.

Here we reconnect to the heart of ourselves and the heart of the land.

# Centennial Supper Club With Michael Robotham

  * Wednesday 14 October 2026
  * 6:30 pm 9:30 pm 18:30 21:30
  * Centennial Vineyards Restaurant (map)
  * Google Calendar ICS

Image

Michael Robotham’s new book is the astonishing, emotional epic Tell Me Something True. It’s a mystery, a coming-of-age tale and a love story wrapped into one, set against the simmering tensions of a small Australian town.

You’re invited to hear all about it from the bestselling, award-winning novelist and master storyteller.

Tickets include drink on arrival, dinner, author talk and book-signing.

## About Tell Me Something True

Small towns are quick to anger and slow to forgive, but Arlo Hackett doesn't expect mercy when he emerges from a twelve-year prison sentence and makes his way back to Yulara, a waypoint on Australia's Great Southern Road. The last time Arlo was home, his brother Luke was charged with a terrible crime and Arlo was found guilty by association. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Update on 3-Parks Monitoring Program: Watarrka National Park -

Phase 1

Page 1 of 28

Summary

• In 2016, the Watarrka National Park Integrated Conservation Strategy (ICS) was finalised and

approved by the Parks and Wildlife Commission of the Northern Territory Government (PWCNT).

• Detailed Biodiversity surveys are a cornerstone of the monitoring and evaluation component of

the ICS.

• The first round of surveys at Watarrka National Park was undertaken by the Department of

Environment and Natural Resources in 2014-2015

1

, with monitoring to be repeated every 3-5

years. Thirty-two permanent sites were established, the locations of which were all approved by

the Park’s Traditional Owners.

• Monitoring is focussed on two of the Park’s identified values – Creeks and Floodouts and Sand

Country – and its aims are to document the flora and fauna of these values, and the impacts of

damaging wildfire, Buffel Grass (and other weeds) and feral herbivores.

• The surveys confirmed that the two values support divergent flora and fauna assemblages and

that tailored approaches to threat management are needed if conservation targets are to be met

over the life of the current ICS.

• For the Creeks and Floodouts, damaging wildfire and Buffel grass have had pronounced impacts

on their current condition, and there is strong evidence that these threatening processes strongly

influence the composition of the plant and animal assemblages present. The prevention of short-

interval fire and the control of Buffel grass around Quandong stands in particular are therefore

confirmed as the highest priority actions.

• For the Sand Country, we confirmed that plant and reptile assemblages correlate closely with fire

for both destructive wildfire and Buffel Grass, and that the highest priority conservation

targets should be set around the management of these threats. In this system, Buffel Grass displaces

native plants and it also increases the frequency and severity of wildfire. Wildfire is, however, also fuelled

by native grasses (principally Themeda triandra) in the rocky sites and so must be understood as part of

the normal functioning of these habitats. Given therefore, the high invasibility and flammability of these
